newsitem.title: ITALY: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Wednesday, October 16.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Wednesday, October 16.

text.p: Following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.
* Italy's highest appeal court, the Court of Cassation, ordered a retrial of former SS captain Erich Priebke (all).
* Opposition Freedom alliance asks Justice minister Giovanni Maria Flick to suspend a Milan magistrate who cast doubts on the integrity of the country's finance police.
* Coalition parties are divided over the proposed removal of the three heads of the secret services (all).
* Freedom alliance leader Silvio Berlusconi appeared as a defence witness in the trial of former Publitalia chairman Marcello Dell'Utri and said the group's accounts are completely clean (all).
* Two people died of heart attacks as an earthquake struck Northern Italy, while floods kill three in the South (all).
* Parliamentary commissions substantially approved the 1997 budget (all).
* Italy's public sector borrowing requirement might total 123 trillion lire at the end of 1996, exceeding by 10 trillion June government forecasts (Sole 24 Ore).

* The privatisation of Banco Napoli will be launched next month. Treasury minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi said the bank was "free from the problems of old management" and added the bid is open to all candidates, domestic and foreign (Sole 24 Ore).
* The Treasury might decide to increase the second tranche share offer of Eni as the roadshow with international investors is seen as successful (Sole 24 Ore).
Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
